text:
A small proposed experiment: cache SASRec, transition, co-occurrence and popularity scores on the identical pinned candidates. Tabulate both-hit, SASRec-only-hit, branch-only-hit and neither-hit outcomes; report ensemble rescues versus regressions. Measure branch coverage as nonzero-score rates for targets and candidates, plus HR@10 conditional on coverage. Ablate transition, co-occurrence and popularity separately; stratify by training-item popularity and history length. Freeze candidate-independent score transforms using training-only reference-score distributions; avoid normalization across the 100 evaluation candidates. Treat these as proposed diagnostics: sampled-candidate rankings can interact with popularity and need not reproduce full-catalog conclusions ([candidate-sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.11723)).

For paired uncertainty, independently resample 200 users with replacement within each dataset, retaining every model’s outcomes for each selected user. Calculate each replicate’s macro difference as one quarter of the sum of four dataset HR@10 differences; report a 95% bootstrap interval and per-dataset deltas. This adapts established [IR bootstrap evaluation](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/ipsjdc/3/0/3_0_625/_article/-char/ja). Intervals condition on fixed candidates and trained models. Predeclare a tiny shared weight grid and checkpoint rule; record every configuration inspected. Bootstrap intervals after selecting the winner do not remove selection optimism. Repeated validation optimization can overfit the selection criterion; treat selected validation gains as exploratory ([Cawley–Talbot](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)).

Compare SASRec BCE, BCE with more negatives, and gBCE with the same increased negative count, architecture and training seed, recording GPU seconds. This separates negative-count effects from loss effects. [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) combines increased negatives with generalized BCE to reduce sampling-induced overconfidence; it does not establish that a transition ensemble will help. Test one preregistered ensemble setting on the strongest neural comparator.
